prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting into trade theory, and so changing how the gains from trade are analysed and taken to firm-level data.

statement.case_for: I keep B001 first on its scientific content, not on how many colleagues ranked it first. Melitz (2003) and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) moved trade analysis from sectors to firms. They gave a tractable account of who exports, who invests abroad, and how trade reallocates resources toward more productive firms. This created a new channel for the gains from trade and a firm-level empirical agenda used across many countries. From my own field, the framework also matters beyond trade. Reallocation and selection are now standard in macro, growth and productivity analysis, and they connect to the firm-dynamics and misallocation work I follow. The core results are more than twenty years old, have been tested repeatedly in firm microdata, and are standard in teaching and policy modelling. The attribution is also the most tractable in the shortlist: Melitz is the originator of the core model, and Helpman co-authored the exporting-versus-FDI extension and has a wider foundational body of trade theory. A two-name award fits the three-laureate limit without forcing contested exclusions of the kind that B024 requires.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution at the edges. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made closely related empirical and theoretical contributions but are outside the credited set, and Redding's quantitative and spatial work is excluded. The committee could reasonably judge that a two-name award under-credits the broader firm-level trade programme. A second concern is that the baseline Melitz model's welfare implications depend on functional-form and distributional assumptions, and some of its detailed predictions have been revised. Finally, trade was recognised with Krugman in 2008, so the committee may weigh how close the new-trade-theory lineage is. I think the conceptual break and the empirical agenda are distinct enough from that earlier recognition.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B001 first for Helpman and Melitz, sees Melitz as originator and Helpman as the broadest contributor, and leaves out Redding as a later extension less central to this discovery. He also flags that the committee might prefer a three-person split.
responses.response: I agree on leaving Redding out. His quantitative and spatial work builds on the framework and extends it, rather than being part of the discovery itself. I would qualify one point. Adding a third name does not solve the attribution problem you raise, because the closest omitted contributors, Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, are not credited on this ballot entry, and adding Redding would not address that gap. I therefore prefer the cleaner two-name award to a third name chosen mainly to fill the cap.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B006 first and B001 second. He argues that BLP and the dynamic oligopoly methods turned structural industrial organisation into a routine tool used in merger review, antitrust, trade and environmental policy, and that the case is fully mature.
responses.response: I agree that B006 is mature and has had large practical reach, and I would not dismiss it as merely methodological. I still rank it below B001 for two reasons. First, the discovery boundary is looser. Demand estimation, production-function estimation and dynamic games are different strands, and the seven credited names show how arbitrary a three-person cut would be, as Hjalmarsson and Friberg also note when they discuss Bresnahan and Reiss. Second, B001 changed what the field asks, namely which firms trade and how reallocation produces gains, and not only how it estimates. That conceptual break is easier to state in a single citation. I accept that the judgment between a conceptual advance and a tool-building contribution is a real difference between us, not a factual one.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B034 second. He regards the Kiyotaki-Moore collateral-constraint mechanism as a clean two-author attribution, deep in theory, and mature after nearly thirty years of use, including after 2008.
responses.response: The attribution is indeed cleaner than in most macro candidates, and I agree the mechanism is foundational. I did not rank it in my top eight, mainly because of the thematic overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises, which Enflo, Fredriksson and Hassler also raise. The empirical identification of the collateral channel is also less direct than the theory. If the committee decides that overlap is not disqualifying, I would regard B034 as a serious alternative. I do not think its attribution advantage outweighs the breadth of reach and the extent of direct empirical confirmation that I see for B001.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the parallel work of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are outside the credited names, as a reason to widen or reframe the trade citation.
Whether Redding's quantitative and spatial contributions should enter the credit, and whether a two-name award is stable against that question.
How much weight Krugman's 2008 recognition should carry for the firm-heterogeneity lineage.
Whether the welfare implications of the heterogeneous-firm framework are robust enough to anchor the citation, given their sensitivity to distributional assumptions.

If B001 is not chosen, I am uncertain which of B035 and B030 is the better fit, since the best-fitting names for B035 are unclear (Saez and Chetty, or others) and the Katz and Dorn question remains open for B030.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Elhanan Helpman or Marc J. Melitz is apparent from the supplied profile, so none bears on the preferred configuration. For transparency, the profile shows a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow (credited in B050, not part of my preferred or alternative parts), frequent co-authorship with Per Krusell and co-authorship with John Hassler, who are IIES colleagues. I also co-authored the Ekonomisk Debatt summaries of the 2024 and 2025 prizes, and the 2025 Scientific Background cites my work. None of these affects B001, B035 or B030 as far as the supplied profile shows. I disclose them and do not adjudicate them.
